name_note: GTDB R232 classifies this species as s__Oscillibacter welbionis; the genomes and the published literature use the name Dysosmobacter welbionis.

sentences.text: Dysosmobacter welbionis is the type species of a genus of strictly anaerobic, butyrate-producing bacteria in the family Oscillospiraceae, described from human faeces.
A review reports that it is carried by roughly two thirds to more than 90% of adults, depending on the cohort and detection method.
That review also reports that its faecal abundance correlates inversely with fasting glucose and glycated haemoglobin.
A study reported a non-canonical myo-inositol-to-butyrate fermentation pathway in this species and reduced abundance in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease across two cohorts.
In high-fat diet-fed mice, administration of the type strain was reported to reduce body weight and fat mass gain and to improve glucose tolerance and insulin resistance.
